idiom_name: hand-written libpact_ffi bindings or Pact-JSON fixtures plus a replay harness
implementation_notes: There is no C DSL for Pact: the shared logic is the Rust core exported through the pact_ffi C ABI, whose header is generated with cbindgen and whose prebuilt libraries are published as the Conan recipes pact_ffi (static) and pact_ffi_dll (dynamic); linking the static library on Linux additionally requires pthread, dl and m. C projects therefore either bind those exported functions by hand to build a mock server from an integration JSON document, or - more commonly - serialize the required interactions to Pact JSON themselves and drive mock and replay with their own HTTP harness. Both routes replace the classic structure (mock server, contract writer, verifier) with hand-written C, so the pattern is realized manually; prefer the FFI route when the contracts must be readable by other Pact implementations rather than only by your own fixtures.
pitfalls: A harness that serves the canned response but never compares the client's actual request turns the mock into a stub: the test stays green even when the client calls the wrong path or method.
Hand-written contracts break silently on JSON escaping, encoding and number formatting; emit them with one serializer and validate them with a second Pact implementation before publishing.
Per-test listeners must bind port 0 and be shut down with close()/shutdown(); a singleton mock reused across tests makes failures order-dependent and hides unmatched interactions.
